significance.justification: Verified true, the claim would establish a form-(iii) predictive coupling: tokens with "higher downstream causal influence and information gain" are more productive, and local activations predict that productivity before completion, thereby constraining which token states should precede useful progress and which tokens can be removed without harming accuracy. This addresses the compute-allocation bottleneck highlighted by process-verification and test-time-scaling work such as Lightman et al. (2023) and Snell et al. (2024), although the proposed signature is principally a behavioral regularity plus causal attribution rather than a detailed mechanism of how reasoning advances. The branches are determinate: a positive result establishes locally observable productivity and its causal relevance, whereas a negative result would meaningfully disfavor token-local monitoring and support non-local or combinatorial accounts of usefulness. After substituting away the specific influence–information-gain coupling, only the generic topic of efficient interpretable reasoning remains and would not earn this score; the specific online predictive law is what places the claim above the topic median.

reach.justification: The named handles are an "online productivity probe from local activations" and the associated ability to "prune unproductive spans"; because the probe predicts productivity "before the trace completes," it is ex ante and leaves an action window for decoding-time pruning or training-time rewards. After per-model re-extraction, the substantive hypothesis still predicts an ordering—productive tokens should have greater causal influence and information gain—but the precise probe and pruning threshold would need recalibration, so transfer is stronger than a one-model direction yet weaker than a quantitative invariant. The hypothesis is phrased broadly over reasoning tokens and could be used by researchers and practitioners optimizing inference, but it does not explicitly guarantee invariance across architectures, scales, task families, or training regimes. Topic substitution would remove the online probe, predictive signature, and pruning handle and therefore would not preserve this score; those claim-specific deliverables, rather than the general importance of efficient reasoning, support the above-median reach.
